items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: like when we would do a concert that had something to do with Rugolo, I would be in his garage for two or three days finding all these original scores

ctx.x: Yeah. And that’s really the key. And again, with your archive of making sure those things are available and having them there for people to access and things like that, that’s so

important. But as you know, that’s not always the case. And a lot of times — and I think the idea behind the whole thing started back in the KLON days when I started to put — not only was I doing the events but also the radio shows that I’ve always done have been more like kind of documentary oriented. And it seems like doing it on a weekly basis that that would be, you know that I’ve, you know, always put a lot of effort into it, a lot of research and I’m kind of built that way in that I always kind of have to…

because people would get very excited over coming to see an alumni band playing. You know it all started with this big Stan Kenton event. I didn’t even intend for that — I never intended for that to be the case. But when I first moved to Los Angeles to take the job at the radio station I got one of the union directories that published Local 47 union directories and I started going through it just to see who was around, and I couldn’t believe that so many of — they still lived in the area, and the one thread that…
